value_stream.name: Strategic Key Account & Enterprise Customer Management

fields.Participants: Merchandising Finance, Account Managers, FP&A (links to VS-17.4), Logistics Finance (links to W277), BI (links to VS-28.1)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Merchandising Finance/BI compute account-level profitability" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "Account Manager analyze profitability drivers" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "Account Manager use profitability analytics to inform pricing/contract renewal" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-552 (ensure controlled execution — Account Profitability, Retention & Strategic Analytics (PA-107.3).)
- operational: driver-based allocation; operational: net-profitability view
Pain Points / Risks: - **Cost-allocation-distortion risk**: Unfair cost-to-serve allocation mis-ranks accounts; mitigated by driver-based allocation
- **Margin-ignoring risk**: Growing revenue at the expense of net contribution (links to VS-101.3); mitigated by net-profitability view
System Touchpoints: - Finance/revenue analytics (links to VS-17.4/VS-101.3); BI (links to VS-28.1); costing (links to VS-85); logistics finance (links to W277); CRM (links to VS-13.3)

steps.activity: Merchandising Finance/BI compute account-level profitability: revenue, GM$ and GM% (net of discounts/rebates links to VS-39/VS-11.1, landed cost links to VS-02.2/VS-87), cost-to-serve (logistics links to VS-06/VS-74/VS-77 staging, special handling, account-team cost, financing/credit cost links to VS-68), returns (links to VS-32), and net contribution; allocate shared costs fairly

Merchandising Finance/Account Manager analyze profitability drivers: product/category mix (links to VS-01/VS-101.3), pricing-vs-tier (links to W3434/VS-01.2), service mix, project margin (links to VS-11.2/VS-40), and cost-to-serve hotspots; flag unprofitable accounts for action

Account Manager use profitability analytics to inform pricing/contract renewal (W3434), mix-shift, service redesign, and tier reassignment (W3425); report profitability to the QBR (W3430) and finance review (links to VS-17.4/VS-101.3)

fields.Participants: Account Manager, Sales Ops, FP&A (links to VS-17.4), Merchandising Finance, CRM (links to VS-13.3)
fields.Trigger: Monthly/quarterly forecast (links to VS-33.2/VS-101); pipeline review

workflows.name: Strategic Account Revenue Forecasting & Pipeline Analytics

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "Account Manager maintain the account pipeline and forecast in CRM" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-validate of "validate against the revenue/margin plan" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-log of "logistics capacity to forecast" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-552 (ensure controlled execution — Account Profitability, Retention & Strategic Analytics (PA-107.3).)
- operational: stage discipline and accuracy tracking; operational: pipeline diversification
Pain Points / Risks: - **Forecast-accuracy risk**: Over-optimistic pipeline distorts the plan and capacity; mitigated by stage discipline and accuracy tracking
- **Concentration risk**: Forecast overly dependent on one deal; mitigated by pipeline diversification
System Touchpoints: - CRM pipeline (links to VS-13.3/W103); FP&A forecast (links to VS-17.4); project pipeline (links to VS-11.2); supply (links to VS-02)

steps.activity: Account Manager maintain the account pipeline and forecast in CRM (links to VS-13.3/W103): qualified opportunities (links to W3433/W3436), stage, probability, value, close-date, and risk; refresh weekly; reconcile to project pipeline (links to VS-11.2/VS-66)

Sales Ops/FP&A aggregate the strategic-account pipeline/forecast, validate against the revenue/margin plan (links to VS-33.1/VS-101.3) and historical accuracy, and identify gaps/concentration/risk; produce the forecast view for executives

steps.a: Head of Trade / Account Management / COO
steps.activity: Account Manager/Head of Strategic Accounts act on forecast risk: accelerate at-risk deals (links to W3436), backfill pipeline gaps, and align supply/logistics capacity to forecast (links to VS-02/VS-06/VS-77); report forecast performance to the executive review (links to VS-33.2)

fields.Participants: Head of Strategic Accounts, Account Managers, Finance (links to VS-17.4), CRM/BI (links to VS-28.1)

workflows.name: Account Performance Scorecard & Tier Health Assessment

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "Accounts/BI publish the account scorecard per account/tier" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "review with Account Managers" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-552 (ensure controlled execution — Account Profitability, Retention & Strategic Analytics (PA-107.3).)
- operational: focused tier-relevant KPIs; operational: balanced scorecard and net-profitability view (W3441)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Metric-overload risk**: Too many scorecard metrics obscure action; mitigated by focused tier-relevant KPIs
- **Gaming risk**: Account managers game metrics; mitigated by balanced scorecard and net-profitability view (W3441)
System Touchpoints: - CRM/BI scorecard (links to VS-13.3/VS-28.1); finance (links to VS-17.4); CSAT (links to VS-13.1); credit (links to VS-68)

steps.activity: Head of Strategic Accounts/BI publish the account scorecard per account/tier: revenue/GM$ vs KAP target (W3427), share-of-wallet (W3433), profitability (W3441), pipeline coverage (W3442), service-level/CSAT (links to VS-13.1/W65), credit/AR health (links to VS-68/VS-16), and at-risk signals (W3446); monthly

steps.a: Head of Trade / Account Management / COO
steps.activity: Head of Strategic Accounts assess tier health: accounts over-/under-performing tier expectations, tier-misalignment candidates (W3425), and resource-allocation adequacy (W3428); recommend re-tier, resource, or intervention

Head of Strategic Accounts conduct the portfolio review with Account Managers: per-account health, action plans, escalations, and resource decisions; track action closure and report portfolio health to executives (links to VS-33.2)

fields.Participants: AR/Credit Manager (links to VS-16/VS-68), Account Manager, Finance (links to VS-17), Treasury (links to VS-18/VS-105)
fields.Trigger: Account credit decision (links to VS-68); portfolio concentration review
fields.Volume: ~5,200 AR accounts; ~200 corporate strategic (links to VS-16.3)

workflows.name: Strategic Account Credit, Concentration & Receivable Risk Management

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "AR/Credit assess strategic-account credit" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-monitor of "monitor concentration risk" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "AR/Credit/Account Manager manage receivable risk on strategic accounts" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-87 (ensure key-account credit concentration & ethics governance.)
- operational: limits and diversification; operational: authority matrix and coordination (W3431)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Concentration risk**: Over-exposure to one account/segment; mitigated by limits and diversification
- **Sales-vs-credit-conflict risk**: Sales pushes credit beyond prudent limits; mitigated by authority matrix and coordination (W3431)
System Touchpoints: - Credit/AR (links to VS-16/VS-68); treasury/concentration (links to VS-18/VS-105); collections (links to VS-16.2); insurance (links to VS-26)

steps.activity: AR/Credit assess strategic-account credit (links to VS-68.1 risk scoring, VS-16.1 credit application): financial health, payment history, project/contract exposure, industry risk, and collateral/guarantees; set/approve credit limit per authority (links to VS-68.2)

Finance/Treasury monitor concentration risk: top-account exposure vs portfolio limits, segment/entity concentration (links to VS-72), and single-name exposure; alert on threshold breach and recommend mitigation (credit reduction, insurance links to VS-26, factoring/SCF links to VS-105)

AR/Credit/Account Manager manage receivable risk on strategic accounts: collection (links to VS-16.2 W108), dispute resolution (links to VS-90/W244), credit-hold coordination with sales (links to W3431), and bad-debt provisioning (links to VS-68.3/W81); report credit risk to the portfolio review (W3443)

fields.Participants: CRM/Analytics (links to VS-13.3/VS-28.1), Merchandising Finance, Account Managers, Data Science (links to VS-30.2)

workflows.name: Customer Lifetime Value (CLV), Retention Economics & Churn Prediction

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "CRM/Analytics compute Customer Lifetime Value" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "Account Manager use CLV/churn insights to prioritize retention" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-552 (ensure controlled execution — Account Profitability, Retention & Strategic Analytics (PA-107.3).)
- operational: conservative assumptions and validation; operational: model refresh and early-warning
Pain Points / Risks: - **CLV-overestimation risk**: Optimistic CLV drives over-investment; mitigated by conservative assumptions and validation
- **Churn-blindspot risk**: Missing behavioral signals delays intervention; mitigated by model refresh and early-warning
System Touchpoints: - CRM/CDP (links to VS-13.3); BI/analytics (links to VS-28.1); data science (links to VS-30.2); CSAT (links to VS-13.1)

steps.activity: CRM/Analytics compute Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) per strategic account: historical margin (W3441), retention horizon, growth trajectory (W3433), cost-to-serve, and discount rate; segment accounts by CLV tier and identify high-value/at-risk

Data Science/Analytics build/maintain churn-prediction and retention-economics models: behavioral signals (declining orders, CSAT drop links to VS-13.1, competitive activity links to VS-57), churn probability, retention cost vs CLV, and intervention ROI; refresh quarterly

Account Manager use CLV/churn insights to prioritize retention (W3446), resource allocation (W3428), and growth investment (W3433); report CLV/churn trends to the portfolio review (W3443) and executives (links to VS-33.2)

fields.Participants: Head of Strategic Accounts, Account Manager, Sponsor, CX (links to VS-13.1), Service (links to VS-12), Customer
fields.Trigger: At-risk signal (W3445/W3443); customer complaint/escalation (links to VS-13.1); lost deal
fields.Volume: ~5–10% of strategic accounts at-risk at any time

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "Account Manager/Analytics identify at-risk accounts from signals" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-track of "Account Manager/Sponsor build and execute the save-plan" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-monitor of "monitor trigger events" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-87 (ensure key-account credit concentration & ethics governance.)
- operational: early-warning analytics (W3445); operational: root-cause discipline and exec engagement
Pain Points / Risks: - **Late-detection risk**: At-risk identified too late to save; mitigated by early-warning analytics (W3445)
- **Ineffective-save risk**: Save-plan doesn't address root cause; mitigated by root-cause discipline and exec engagement
System Touchpoints: - CRM (links to VS-13.3); CX/complaint (links to VS-13.1/W469); analytics (links to VS-28.1); service (links to VS-12/VS-90)

steps.activity: Account Manager/Analytics identify at-risk accounts from signals: declining revenue/order, CSAT drop (links to VS-13.1/W65), complaint escalation (links to W469/W41), competitive displacement (links to VS-57), stakeholder turnover (W3429), credit-hold friction (W3444); classify root cause and severity

Account Manager/Sponsor build and execute the save-plan: root-cause resolution (service issue links to VS-12/VS-90, pricing links to W3434, relationship links to W3429), executive intervention (W3438), concession within authority, and demonstrated recovery; track save-progress

For churned/lapsed accounts, Account Manager maintain the win-back plan: periodic re-engagement, monitor trigger events (new project, competitor failure), and reactivate (links to VS-13.1 W84 reactivation); capture loss lessons (W3447) and feed to continuous improvement

fields.Participants: Head of Strategic Accounts, Account Manager, Competitive Intel (links to VS-57/VS-33.3), Merchandising (links to VS-01), Service (links to VS-12)
fields.Trigger: Lost strategic account or major deal

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "Account Manager conduct the loss review" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "Accounts/CI aggregate loss patterns across the portfolio" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "report loss analysis and remediation to executives" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-552 (ensure controlled execution — Account Profitability, Retention & Strategic Analytics (PA-107.3).)
- operational: rigorous loss review; operational: systemic remediation tracking and exec reporting
Pain Points / Risks: - **Root-cause-masking risk**: Blaming "price" masks underlying service/relationship issues; mitigated by rigorous loss review
- **Inaction risk**: Loss lessons not remediated; mitigated by systemic remediation tracking and exec reporting
System Touchpoints: - CRM (links to VS-13.3); competitive intel (links to VS-57/VS-33.3); pricing/assortment (links to VS-01); service (links to VS-12)

steps.activity: Account Manager conduct the loss review: root cause (price links to VS-01.2, product/assortment links to VS-01, service links to VS-12, relationship links to W3429, credit links to VS-68, competitor offer links to VS-57), decision process, and what would have changed the outcome; document findings

Head of Strategic Accounts/CI aggregate loss patterns across the portfolio: recurring root causes, competitor tactics, segment/category concentration, and disintermediation signals (e.g., customer direct-import links to VS-87); identify systemic issues

steps.a: Head of Trade / Account Management / COO
steps.activity: Head of Strategic Accounts drive systemic remediation: pricing/assortment/service fixes (links to VS-01/VS-12), competitive response (links to VS-57/W329), training (links to VS-43.3/VS-19.4), and process improvement; report loss analysis and remediation to executives (links to VS-33.2) and feed to the KAP cycle (W3427)

fields.Participants: Head of Strategic Accounts, Finance (links to VS-17.4), Head of Trade / Account Management, CFO, Board (links to VS-36)
fields.Trigger: Quarterly/annual program review; board cycle (links to VS-36)

workflows.name: KAM Program Performance, ROI & Executive/Board Reporting

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "Accounts/Finance compile the KAM program performance view" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-report of "report KAM program performance, strategic-account concentration, and risk to…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-552 (ensure controlled execution — Account Profitability, Retention & Strategic Analytics (PA-107.3).)
- operational: finance review and audit; operational: ROI analytics
Pain Points / Risks: - **Concentration-disclosure risk**: Material customer concentration undisclosed/mis-stated; mitigated by finance review and audit
- **Program-ROI-blindspot risk**: Program cost not measured against outcome; mitigated by ROI analytics
System Touchpoints: - Finance/analytics (links to VS-17.4/VS-28.1); CRM (links to VS-13.3); executive reporting (links to VS-33.2); board (links to VS-36); incentives (links to W228/VS-102.3)

steps.a: Head of Trade / Account Management / CFO
steps.activity: Head of Strategic Accounts/Finance compile the KAM program performance view: strategic-account revenue/GM$ and share of total, growth vs market, retention/churn (W3445), profitability (W3441), pipeline coverage (W3442), program cost (account teams W3428) and ROI, and strategic-account concentration risk (W3444)

Head of Strategic Accounts/CFO evaluate program effectiveness vs objectives and strategy (links to VS-33): tier coverage adequacy, resource productivity, growth/retention outcome, and competitor position; recommend program adjustments (coverage, team model, incentives links to W228/VS-102.3)

CFO/Head of Strategic Accounts report KAM program performance, strategic-account concentration, and risk to the executive committee (links to VS-33.2) and Board (links to VS-36); ensure disclosure of material customer concentration in financial reporting (links to VS-17) and alignment with the revenue/margin narrative (links to VS-101.3)
